steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Can I start now? I thought I saw the record button flash for a moment, but it might've just been my imagination. Oh... feels like it's starting to warm up... so I guess it's working?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ahem, well then... Today is the third day of the field expedition, and we've almost made it to the survey site.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The time now is ten thirty... is that a one? Sorry, I can't see very clearly, but it's morning.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Oh, it-it's a two now! The time is 10:32, and our ETA to the rendezvous point with Rhodes Island is... Umm, twelve hours and twenty-eight minutes.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Everything has been going smoothly so far, and the detection rune is ready. As for the sampling equipment, the others are currently helping me with it.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Umm, what was that? I thought I heard someone calling me...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ack, I almost dropped the recorder. Phew... Okay, don't panic...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Are they waving at me? I think that signal means they finished the installation? Begin data collection... Begin synchronous analysis... G-Got it!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Eyjafjalla!

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Oh... Um, Barty? Hearing aids... Okay, my hearing aids are working fine.

steps.name: Barty
steps.text: Woah, hold on, there's no rush! Please mind your step.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I-It's fine... Barty, I can walk on my own. The visibility here is very good, so you don't need to worry about me running into things.

steps.name: Barty
steps.text: You sure? The wind's pretty strong out here though, and there are rocks jutting out all over the place. Wouldn't it be better for you to stay on the aircraft?

steps.name: Barty
steps.text: Besides, when I left, I told Dr. Kal'tsit I would keep you safe. Bet my whole next month's salary on it.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ughh......

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Salad? With... Dr. Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Huh? No, I said salary, my salary!

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: (whispers) Like hell I'd ask Dr. Kal'tsit to share a salad...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Oh, umm, I see...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ugh... My hearing aid... I'm sure there must be some interference, maybe because the wind is too strong.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I'm very sorry. You were just talking about your work, right?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I know how reliable you are, Barty. You've been a great help to me on this trip. If I was alone here, even setting up this equipment would've taken all afternoon.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Huh, by yourself? You really think you could've handled all this heavy equipment? Even given a whole afternoon...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I've done it before. Back when I was in school, there were some research projects I had to carry out by myself.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Huh, what about your classmates?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ah, well... Everyone took it differently... Those courses, they did require a bit more experience.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Right, I almost forgot through all that small talk, you're a real accomplished scholar. I guess the other students couldn't keep up with you?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: But even so, they were working you way too hard back in school.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: It actually wasn't that bad... S-Seriously, don't worry about it. I can handle myself, I just take my time.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But you know, after coming to Rhodes Island, it is much more convenient to get things done, whether on the landship or out in the field.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: My new hearing aids are a lot better than the ones I was using before. Dr. Kal'tsit and the Professor are both supportive of my research, and Closure even helped me renovate my room...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The other operators always take very good care of me, just like you are now. I'm so glad I have all of you.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: You thanked me the whole way here. C'mon, you're gonna make me blush.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Hey! I just came back from there. The road's real narrow, so while y'all can still pass, that heavy thing's gotta stay behind.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ugh... Does that mean there's no way for us to get to the last sampling point?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: I said, y'all can pass. You— can— pass—.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Look, there's no need to raise your voice, okay?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: She's just standin' there all confused. Her ears bad or something?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Sorry... I heard you this time.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Um, Barty, let's go take a look first?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Wait, hold up, you're going too? I did say it's clear, but don't you think it'd be better for someone like you to take it easy?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: The road up ahead is pretty nasty. A lot of earthquakes hit this area, and there are pits and sinkholes everywhere. One wrong move and you're stuck in one of those. Wouldn't even come out here if not for the money.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Lookin' at you, you're havin' a tough time just walkin' on flat ground, and now you wanna join in on this craziness? Isn't that just looking for trouble?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: You... How dare you talk like that to Eyjafjalla! She may be young, but she's the greatest volcanologist in the world! She's in charge of this whole expedition!

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Volcanology gonna pick her up and carry her? The only thing gettin' you across this road is a sturdy pair o' legs.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: I guess you have a point... Um, Eyjafjalla... He's kinda right. If the road ahead is really that rough, you should...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Barty, Mr. Guide, I am very sorry... for causing you trouble.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But, I need to go.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: If you're concerned about the equipment, I can set it up for you—

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Yes, I know. What you said is true. But, the source of the anomalous Originium readings is right up ahead. We need more precise detection method, and that requires my Arts.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Why not use the data from the sampling sites? There's a lot to pick from, right?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: No good. We can't overlook even the smallest detail if we want accurate results. If I get lazy here, our entire mission may fall short.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: I know that serious look, you've made up your mind... then we've got no choice. Let's go.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: But let me get this out of the way, Eyjafjalla, if you ever feel uncomfortable, we're going to stop to take a break. You've got a duty to your research, but I've got a duty to protect you.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Okay... I'll be fine, Barty. Don't worry about me.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: *Sigh*... I can tell you're pushing yourself!

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Tsk... If you don't like hearing the truth...

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Let me just make this clear. If somethin' happens, I'm only gonna be lookin' after myself.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Damn it, people like you...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: It's fine, don't worry about it. Thank you for showing us the way, Mr. Guide.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Continuing recording... The current time is 12:25 P.M., and we're moving towards the last sampling site.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: We've analyzed the data from the previous sampling site and... Well, it's pretty much what I predicted.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Despite being igneous rock deposited by an ancient volcano, there's still strong Originium activity deep within it. It continues to grow stronger, and the trend is... undeniable.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The key lies in the core of the anomalous band... With that data, we'll be able to analyze the trajectory of change... I hope it won't interfere with Rhodes Island's subsequent— Eek!

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I, I just bumped my shoulder on something... Sorry, Barty... I wasn't watching where I was going.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Is everything okay? We've been walking for an hour already.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ah... Um... Yeah, I'm fine.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: The wind is really strong here, stronger than before. It's making its way into the cracks of the rocks, just like us.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Yeah... It's really cold... My legs are all sore, and my eyes...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But, I can do this. Please keep going.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: You're really not going to let anything stop you, huh?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Tell you what. You stand behind me, I'm big enough to block the wind for you. If there are any rocks, I'll get us out of the way.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Okay... Sounds good. Thank you, Barty.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Hey... Don't say I didn't warn you. This road's hard to get through.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: So, what kind of treasure are you lookin' for? Must be great to get you pushin' through all this.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: I think we told you back when we hired you? We're from Rhodes Island, a pharmaceutical company, and we're here to investigate and research—

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Yeah, yeah, I heard all that before.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: But like what investigation, what research? Isn't it all about money in the end?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Heh, especially pharmaceutical companies like yours. I bet you've squeezed a whole lot of old rich folk desperately trying to survive, right?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: You... you wouldn't get it.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: There's nothing wrong with trying to make money, but some things you can't put a price on.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Hm? Not here for money then? I was gonna say... how'd you plan to make money digging for rocks?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Right, now that I think about it, there are some people, underlings working for those old aristocrats, always trying to play around with Arts. Always experimenting with things, researching things...

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Terrible... just terrible...

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Hey you... Why are you trembling? I told you already, we're nothing like that...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: *gasp*... Wooahhh! What the hell is that massive boulder?!

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: My head... My head... Oh, it's still there?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Wasn't that huge boulder flying towards my head just a moment ago? I thought I was a goner for sure...

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Ow, what's this red stuff? And what's with the debris all over the ground? This bubbly stuff... magma? From a volcano?

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Did the volcano erupt?! H-Help! I don't wanna die!

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Shut up already!

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Damn, I've been wanting to say that for the longest time...

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Eyjafjalla... Eyjafjalla?! Are you all right?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Are you looking for me, Barty? I'm perfectly fine, right over here. Nobody got hurt by that falling boulder just now, right?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: I think we're all okay. When I saw that thing coming at us, I thought it was too late— Wait, did you destroy that boulder with your Arts?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Yes. As long as everyone's safe.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Incredible... Even I didn't have a chance to react... And despite your eyes and ears...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: You're right, Barty. I didn't hear anything. And I only vaguely saw a shadow.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But what I could feel... was the change in heat.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: As Mr. Guide here also mentioned, the stone here is unstable. When affected by the strong winds, the rock formation fractures, and the friction between the fault and the rock mass generates a significant amount of heat.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Wow! Eyjafjalla, you're awesome, really!

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Amazing... and kinda scary...

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: In just a flash, a single moment! That huge boulder, reduced to molten fragments!

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: My god... if that thing had smashed into my head—

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Got it, shutting up. Shutting up.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ah, we've finally arrived.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Right now it's... Oh, we're fifteen minutes behind schedule. Let's pick up the pace.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Booting up the equipment... still need to improve accuracy by fifteen percent... Frequency control, oscillating flow rate... Okay... Nine percent... Three percent...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Great, noise readings are into the ideal range. Barty, you can let go now.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: This... this is also Arts?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Yes, this indeed is my Originium technique. You can think of it as Arts, but I prefer to call it a scientific research method.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Incredible...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Mr. Guide, you must be tired as well? We can head up and rest for a bit. Sample collection will take a while to finish, so we'll have about five hours before we have to check back on the equipment.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: So this is a scientist... A real scientist. Even though she's so young, she's got some real weighty words.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Also, you just saved my life. And I'm the kind of person who knows a good one.

steps.name: Guide
steps.text: Tell you what, I'll take the prepaid part of the guide fee. You don't have to pay the rest.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Look, how many times do we have to tell you... Rhodes Island isn't that stingy—

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Mm... Um, Barty... If Mr. Guide insists, I think we should accept his gratitude.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Huh? Oh, I see... Well, if you say so, Eyjafjalla, I guess we could do that.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: (low voice) I must say, I'm a little surprised...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: What did you say, Barty? Sorry, but I couldn't hear you clearly.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Haha, it's nothing. I'm just saying, I didn't expect you to be so perceptive about this kind of stuff.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Huh? Actually... it's kind of awkward when you put it that way...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I guess I don't really understand what Mr. Guide is talking about.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: In any case... Um, my hearing aids still don't work very well... But Mr. Guide looked really sincere and seemed to be thanking us...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Did I misunderstand something?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: I guess not... Ahaha... You really are a true scholar, aren't you?

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: You can look past the superficial noise and cut straight to the truth at just a glance.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Errmmm... O-Okay...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The time is now 3:14 P.M. Data collection and analysis are progressing steadily.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: A small incident occurred just now on the way to the last sampling site. Of course, it hasn't affected our work.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I also had some interesting conversations with Mr. Guide and Operator Barty along the way...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Even though I'm not sure I understood everything they meant, I think Barty said I'm a true scholar...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I blushed a little when I heard that... and it also made me think of something that happened before I left.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I won't allow it! Eyjafjalla, given your physical condition, you are forbidden to work outdoors again!

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: B-But... the anomalous Originium signal is likely related to volcanic activity, and it happens to be situated on Rhodes Island's next route.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Both as a volcanologist and as an Operator of Rhodes Island, I must complete this field survey.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But your health...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Please have faith in me. I know how to take care of myself.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Let her go.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Huh? Ceylon? You're a medic. How can you support the patient's irresponsible actions?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Sure, even if it's irresponsible...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I also consider myself an academic of sorts, so I can kind of understand how she feels.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: In other words, if I was given an opportunity to learn more about Originium, I'd definitely do everything within my power to make that happen.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I know, but... I'm just worried that another mission would worsen her condition further.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: That would make me want to go even more.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Time is short, but the truth is still far away— and that's why we're even more eager to seize every opportunity, every day.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: While I still can... while my legs can still support me... While my eyes... can still see that light... the brightness of the volcanoes.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Yes, those lights... A an armchair scientist like me might not be able to see them, but I know Eyjafjalla can.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Scholars like her have always been on the bleeding edge, pushing this world's knowledge forward. Every time she can move forward is another step that we'll be able to follow.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Moving forward may not always be a good thing. It might be scary, and it might trip you up. But I'm not going to stop Eyjafjalla's progress just because I'm worried she'll get hurt.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Whatever... I'll never understand you academic types.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Alright, if you insist, Eyjafjalla, I won't try to stop you. You'll have to take it up with Dr. Kal'tsit!

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Right... Thank you. Thank you so much, and you as well, Miss Ceylon.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: That was the same topic back there.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: What does it mean to be a scholar, a scientist? I don't think I've ever given this much thought.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ceylon was right. I wanted to delve deeper into these volcanoes, to explore the mystery of the deepest parts of this land while I still have the time.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: When I was young, if I had to think of what was a true scholar, I would have thought of my mom and dad...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: But now, there's one more person.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: So, can you tell me the answer to this question when I get back—— Professor?
